note.question: Can competing firms using only their own revenue gradients learn prices that are both Nash optimal and dynamically stable when consumer reference prices evolve over time?
note.overview: Competing firms repeatedly choose prices under MNL demand and memory-based reference effects; the paper proves that decentralized first-order learning converges to stationary Nash equilibrium under loss-neutral and loss-averse regimes.

components.label: Stationary Nash equilibrium with decentralized no-regret learning
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Stationary Nash equilibrium with decentralized no-regret learning. An SNE is the fixed point p^E(p*)=p*, so each firm's price is a best response when current and reference prices coincide and the state remains stable thereafter. The paper proves convergence to the unique SNE or SNE set under its loss-neutral and loss-averse conditions.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At each discrete period, firms simultaneously post prices without observing current rivals' prices. Consumers choose under MNL utility with current and reference prices. Revenues and own first-order feedback are observed, reference prices update by exponential smoothing, and firms apply OPGA or its conservative loss-averse variant for the next period. Each period's posted price changes the future reference state as well as current demand.

components.explanation: The authors analyze nonlinear MNL revenue and reference-state dynamics, establish SNE properties, design projected-gradient algorithms using firm-local feedback, prove last-iterate convergence and regret bounds, and test trajectories numerically under several robustness variants.
